chunks: Why N-type has lower resistance. The question: Why do N-type semiconductors typically have lower resistance?
N-type silicon has lower resistance than P-type silicon when both are doped by the same amount. Resistance depends on how many carriers there are and how fast each one moves.
With equal doping, the counts are about equal. But electrons move faster than holes, so N-type conducts better.
Picture two toll roads with the same number of cars. On one road the cars drive at 60 km/h and on the other they crawl at 20 km/h.
In an hour, the faster road moves more cars past the booth, so it carries more traffic. Equal car counts, different speeds, different flow. The analogy holds at equal doping.
At very heavy doping, the crowd of impurity atoms slows both kinds of carrier, and the speed gap shrinks.
At light doping the ratio sits near the lightly doped mobility ratio.
As ionized-impurity scattering takes over (above about 10 to the 17 ), both mobilities converge toward their minimum values and the ratio decreases.
It never reaches 1 in this model; heavily doped P-type is still more resistive than N-type at equal doping.
Conductivity ( ): how well a material carries current, equals q n micro : charge per carrier, times carrier count, times mobility. Higher means lower resistance.
Resistivity ( ): the opposite of conductivity, 1 over , in ohm-cm. Mobility ( micro ): how fast carriers move per unit of field.
Majority carrier density: about equal to the doping level. Doping level: dopant atoms per cm³.
Dope two pieces of silicon, one N-type and one P-type, each with 10 to the 16 atoms per cm³. The carrier counts are both about 10 to the 16 .
At this doping, electron mobility is about 1220 and hole mobility about 437, a bit below the 1350 and 480 of very lightly doped silicon. The ratio is still about 2.
8, so the N-type resistivity is about 2. 8 times lower: about 0. 51 ohm-cm for N-type against about 1. 43 ohm-cm for P-type. That is the whole idea.
"Conductivity is q(n micro n plus p micro p) . At the same doping, N-type and P-type have the same majority density, but electron mobility (about 1350 cm²/V·s) is around 2.
8 times the hole mobility (about 480). So N-type conducts about 2. 8 times better. At 10 to the 16 per cm³ that's about 0. 5 ohms·cm versus 1. 5 ohms·cm.
It narrows at heavy doping, and it only holds at equal doping."
